chunks: He said: Abu Ubaidullah Muhammad ibn Imran al-Marzbani reported to me from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, who reported from Abdullah ibn Abu Saeed al-Warraq, who reported from Masood ibn Amru al-Jahdari, from Ibrahim ibn Dahah, who said:
The first elegy recited for al-Husayn ibn Ali, peace be upon them both, was by Aqabah ibn Amru al-Sahmi, from the tribe of Banu Sahm ibn Awf ibn Ghalib:

"When the eye was content in this life and you fear in this world, as its light has turned into darkness. I passed by the grave of al-Husayn at Karbala, my tears rolled down copiously. I have not stopped lamenting and weeping in sorrow, my eyes helped by their tears and sighing. I wept after al-Husayn for groups whose graves surround him on both sides. Peace upon the interred at Karbala, and say my peace visiting them. Peace in the evenings and at midmorning, conveyed by the winds and their dust. And may visitors never cease coming to his grave, whose musk and fragrance exudes to them."

key_terms.بِكَرْبَلَا: at Karbala, site of al-Husayn's martyrdom

ai.seo_question: What was the first elegy composed for al-Husayn ibn Ali after Karbala?
ai.summary: This hadith identifies the first elegy ever composed for al-Husayn ibn Ali after his martyrdom at Karbala. The poet Aqabah ibn Amru al-Sahmi describes passing by al-Husayn's grave and weeping copiously, offering salutations to all the martyrs buried at Karbala, and expressing hope that visitors will never cease coming to the fragrant shrine.
